top_comments.text:
This is crazy.

I could see multiple plan changes if they were for the better.

But there really is no reason why these language models should be so costly in system resources.

The only possible cause for the expense is the fact of the pile of informational trash that it must process each and every time!

Decrease that trash pile, reduce the compute cost!

I like a really good laugh. Like how the experts have designed the “Multitude of Experts” or MoE.

The latest model that I heard about only activates 16 of over a thousand, nearly two thousand experts.

Think about what that really means.

You stuff about two thousand people into a rather small and crowded space and try to have an intelligent conversation with just 16 people out of that entire massive group!

If anyone in real life suggested something like that, they would give them a new white suit jacket and place em in a bouncy room!

Who in their right mind would even consider having a serious conversation in such a massive crowd?

How would it be possible to concentrate and filter out all of that background noise?

I’m not even sure if I could breathe in a room like that, if I wanted to!

Imagine all the bad gas if they all ate beans.

That is just how bad a situation like this stinks!

I used to work for a while as a Stamp Press operator with multiple multi ton machines banging to produce some ultra high quality noise. The kind of noise you’d love to escape!

The funny part is that a group of engineers would never share the same space for their routine work on a continuous basis!

So, why would anyone expect to do this kind of thing with AI?

Is it any wonder why AI suffer from so much drift or hallucinations?

Why don’t we use that real life common sense and apply it to AI?

It really isn’t all that difficult. 

It is difficult if it is planned for!

And if planned for, it is more efficient and less costly to put into practice!

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Love that analogy, cramming 2000 "experts" in a room and only letting 16 talk is chaos, no wonder we get drift and high costs. If we built AI more like focused teams instead of a noisy stadium, do you think we’d get cleaner results for less compute?
